venue: Yankee Stadium (Bronx, New York, NY). CONFIRMED as the New York Yankees' current and only home ballpark for the 2026 season. NO rename and NO relocation. Ballparks of Baseball, Facts & Figures, states verbatim '-Former Name(s): None' and '-Naming Rights: None - Named after the Yankees' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/yankee-stadium/), so there is no stadium naming right and no field naming right to confuse (contrast Daikin Park, Rate Field, UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium). Wikipedia's '2026 New York Yankees season' article gives the 2026 home ballpark as 'Yankee Stadium' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_New_York_Yankees_season). The team's own site serves the 2026 ballpark pages under mlb.com/yankees/ballpark/* using the name 'Yankee Stadium' (https://www.mlb.com/yankees/ballpark/netting, https://www.mlb.com/yankees/ballpark/information/disabled-services). Ticketmaster lists the venue as 'Yankee Stadium - Bronx, NY' for the 2026-2027 event schedule (https://www.ticketmaster.com/yankee-stadium-tickets-bronx/venue/237572). This is the 2009 ballpark ('-Opened: April 16, 2009', Ballparks of Baseball), NOT the 1923 Yankee Stadium, which was demolished; any source describing the 1923 building (e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium_(1923)) is STALE for this project. STALE-SOURCE WARNING: interior sponsor names have changed and older guides are out of date on them - the current official accessibility page names a 'Coupa Suite Level', an 'Audi Yankees Club' and a 'DigaCore Banquet & Conference Center', while RateYourSeats section pages still use older names such as 'Delta Sky360 Suite', 'Jim Beam Suite', 'Pepsi Lounge' and 'Ford Field MVP Club Lounge'. These are club/lounge sponsorships INSIDE the park; none of them is a stadium or field naming right and none changes the venue name. UNVERIFIED: a low-quality aggregator (https://sportsradioservice.com/2025/05/28/thats-amaury-news-and-commentary-yankees-announced-6-4-billion-stadium-renovation/) refers to a '$6.4 Billion Stadium renovation'; this was NOT corroborated by mlb.com or any primary source and MUST NOT be treated as affecting 2026 seating. Treat as UNKNOWN.

orientation.note: No source consulted states a compass bearing for Yankee Stadium. Baseball Almanac's American League ballpark-orientation page (https://www.baseball-almanac.com/stadium/ballpark_NSEW_AL.shtml) renders its orientation as an image/compass rose that could not be read as text. Ballparks.com's orientation table (https://ballparks.com/baseball/general/facts/diamonds/index.htm) returned only the generic Official Baseball Rules quotation that the line from home base through the pitcher's plate to second base 'shall run East Northeast', with no per-park value for Yankee Stadium. wherestheshade.com (https://wherestheshade.com/mlb-stadium-orientation) discusses the north/northeast tendency but gives no Yankee Stadium bearing.
orientation.weak_indication: UNVERIFIED and NOT to be relied on: a RateYourSeats section-236 page description of the left-field bleachers was rendered as 'Completely uncovered and West-facing' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/236). If those seats face west toward home plate, home plate lies west/southwest of left field and the diamond points roughly east-northeast, consistent with the general MLB rule. orientation.internal_geography_confirmed: The relative geography IS firmly established even without a compass bearing: right field / first-base side holds the LOW section numbers and left field / third-base side holds the HIGH section numbers at every tier (see numbering_direction).

numbering_direction.sweeps: YES - Yankee Stadium sweeps ONE WAY continuously around the bowl. It is NOT a parity/outward-from-home-plate park.
numbering_direction.direction: Section numbers INCREASE from the RIGHT FIELD / FIRST BASE side, around behind home plate, toward the LEFT FIELD / THIRD BASE side. Equivalently: low numbers = right field / first base; high numbers = left field / third base. This holds independently on every tier (field/Legends 11-29, Field Level 103-136, Main Level + Bleachers 201-239, Terrace 305-334, Grandstand 405-434).
numbering_direction.parity_check: NO PARITY SIGNATURE FOUND. The Yankees' official netting page states a SINGLE CONTINUOUS RANGE - 'between Section 011 on the 1st base/right field side of the Stadium and continues to Section 029 on the 3rd base/left field side' - not the two-range odd/even form ('111-115 on the first base side and 112-116 on the third base side') that marks the parity parks. Every other confirmed anchor below is also consistent with a single monotonic sweep. The generator's existing single-sweep config schema applies; no parity handling is needed at Yankee Stadium.

numbering_direction.cross_check_geometry: The bullpen and foul-pole statements corroborate the direction and are internally consistent. RateYourSeats: 'Some fans have complained about the foul poles in Sections 107 and 132' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/107) - so 107 and 132 straddle the infield, and 103-106 / 133-136 are the fair-territory outfield sections beyond each pole, with 103 and 136 the closest to center field. RateYourSeats: 'The Yankees Bullpen is to the Right of Section 103' and 'To sit near the Yankees bullpen, sit in seat 1 on the right-side of Section 103' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/103); 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is to the Left of Section 136' and 'Alternatively, sitting in a high-number seat in Section 136 will have you next to the Visitor's bullpen' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/136); 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is in Front of Section 237 and 238' and 'Section 237 and 238 look directly down into the visitors' bullpen' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/237). Since 237-238 are confirmed LEFT FIELD bleachers by the same page, the visitors' bullpen is in LEFT-center - which places section 136 (adjacent to it) in LEFT field and section 103 (adjacent to the Yankees bullpen) in RIGHT field. Every statement lands the same way.
numbering_direction.confidence: HIGH. Three official (mlb.com netting) anchors plus five independent RateYourSeats anchors plus bullpen/foul-pole geometry, with zero contradicting statements. NO source anywhere asserts the opposite sweep.

dugouts.CONFLICT_FLAG: A RateYourSeats sentence, printed verbatim on several Field MVP section pages (119, 121B and others), reads: 'Field MVP seating spans Sections 115 through 125, wrapping around the infield from behind the visitors' dugout to the home dugout.' Because section numbers increase from the first-base/right-field side toward the third-base/left-field side (see numbering_direction), reading that sentence as an ordered sweep would put the VISITORS' dugout near section 115 on the FIRST BASE side and the HOME dugout near section 125 on the THIRD BASE side - the OPPOSITE of Ballparks of Baseball and Event Ticket Center. The sentence may instead be describing only the extent of the zone without implying an order. BOTH readings are recorded here; the conflict is repeated in `uncertain`. DO NOT reconcile. The two dedicated dugout sources agree with each other and are treated as the stronger evidence, but the ambiguity is genuine and unresolved. This is exactly the failure mode called out in the brief (a popular stadium guide inverted the dugouts at Progressive Field), so the dugout side MUST be re-verified against a photograph or the official seating map before any seat-level output depends on it.

bullpens: BOTH bullpens are beyond the outfield fence in center field, flanking Monument Park - NOT along the foul lines. YANKEES (home) bullpen: RIGHT-CENTER field, immediately beyond section 103. RateYourSeats verbatim: 'The Yankees Bullpen is to the Right of Section 103 - Sitting in Seat 1 will have you right up against the wall overlooking the Yankees bullpen.' and 'To sit near the Yankees bullpen, sit in seat 1 on the right-side of Section 103.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/103). VISITORS' bullpen: LEFT-CENTER field, beyond section 136 and directly below bleacher sections 237-238. RateYourSeats verbatim: 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is to the Left of Section 136' and 'Alternatively, sitting in a high-number seat in Section 136 will have you next to the Visitor's bullpen.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/136); 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is in Front of Section 237 and 238' and 'Section 237 and 238 look directly down into the visitors' bullpen' and 'Monument Park Proximity: These sections are located directly above the famous Monument Park' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/237). Wikipedia adds that 'The Yankees' bullpen connects to Monument Park via a door' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium). NOTE: the three RateYourSeats bullpen statements are mutually consistent and consistent with the confirmed numbering direction, so this is treated as reliable, but no OFFICIAL Yankees page stating bullpen sides was found - re-verify if a seat-level claim depends on it.

accessibility: Source: New York Yankees official 'Yankee Stadium Guide For Guests With Disabilities' (https://www.mlb.com/yankees/ballpark/information/disabled-services). ACCESSIBLE SEATING: wheelchair accessible and designated aisle-transfer seats are stated to be available at various price points and locations throughout the Stadium; the page does NOT enumerate the accessible sections, directing guests to Disabled Services instead. ELEVATORS - 16 public elevators: Gate 2 Lobby, two elevators, serving the Coupa Suite Level, Main and Terrace/Grandstand Levels, the Audi Yankees Club and the Budweiser Hall of Fame Lounge; Suite Entrance near Gate 4, two elevators, serving the suite levels and the Great Hall Landing Bar; Great Hall, eight elevators, serving the Main and Terrace/Grandstand Levels; Gate 6, two elevators, serving the Yankees Steakhouse, Museum, Party Suites and DigaCore Banquet & Conference Center; Gate 8, two elevators, serving the FIELD LEVEL and the BLEACHERS. RAMPS - two accessible ramps inside the Stadium, one 'adjacent to Gate 2 on the left-field side' and one 'adjacent to Gate 6 on the right-field side'. GATE GEOMETRY CROSS-CHECK (hard fact, per the brief): Gate 2 = LEFT-FIELD side and Gate 6 = RIGHT-FIELD side. ELECTRICAL OUTLETS are listed as available at Guest Relations Booths and at these wheelchair-accessible seating sections, which is the closest thing to a published accessible-section list: 021B, 029, 104-106, 109, 111, 114A, 116, 118-121B, 124, 127A, 130, 132-134, 211, 225, 226, 305-310, 313-315, 317-320A, 320C-323, 325-327, 330-331, 333-334, and Bleachers 203, 235-237. Note this list uses the LEADING-ZERO spelling ('021B', '029') for field-level sections. CONTACT: Disabled Services (718) 579-4510 voice, (718) 579-4595 TTY, disabledservices@yankees.com. Wikipedia adds the building has '16 passenger elevators' and an improved restroom fixture ratio of '1 per 60 fans versus 1 per 89 in the original stadium' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium). NOT STATED anywhere consulted: companion-seat counts, accessible-seat totals, or accessible parking specifics - UNKNOWN.
row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE NUMBERED, not lettered, at every tier examined, starting at Row 1 at the front and increasing away from the field. Observed ranges: field-level outfield section 103 'Rows in Section 103 are labeled 1-10'; section 104 'Rows in Section 104 are labeled 1-18'; section 134 'Rows in Section 134 are labeled 1-18'; section 136 'Rows in Section 136 are labeled 1-9'; Field MVP section 115 'Rows in Section 115 are labeled 1-19', section 119 'Rows in Section 119 are labeled 1-17', section 125 'Rows in Section 125 are labeled 1-19', sections 120A/120B/121B 'Rows in Section 120A are labeled 1-17'; Main Level section 205 'Rows in Section 205 are labeled 1-22'; Bleachers section 201 'Rows in Section 201 are labeled 1-24', section 239 'Rows in Section 239 are labeled 1-24'; Terrace section 320B 'Rows in Section 320B are labeled 1-10'; Grandstand sections 418/420B/405 'Rows ... are labeled 1-14'. SPECIAL ROW-LABEL SUFFIXES - THIS IS THE ACCESSIBLE-ROW CONVENTION: (a) 'WC' marks the wheelchair row - Terrace sections 305, 318 and 334 are labeled 'Rows 1-7, 8WC, 9SR' and Delta Sky360 section 220B is labeled 'Rows 1-7, 8WC'. (b) 'SR' marks the standing-room row behind it - '9SR', with RateYourSeats noting 'standing room only space behind Row 8WC and an entrance at Row 9SR' at section 334. (c) 'W' is used instead of 'WC' in the Bleachers - section 203 is labeled 'Rows 1-20, 21W'. So a Terrace-level section typically runs 1..7, 8WC, 9SR and a bleacher section runs 1..20, 21W. ENTRANCE ROWS are stated per section (e.g. 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 18' at section 104, 'at Row 10' at section 103, 'at Row 24' at section 201, 'at Row 17' at sections 120A/120B). SEAT NUMBERS run 1..N within each row with no gaps observed; per-row seat counts vary and are published per section (e.g. section 104: 'Rows 1-2 have 20 seats labeled 1-20', 'Rows 3-10 have 24 seats labeled 1-24', tapering to 'Row 17 has 5 seats labeled 1-5'). COVERAGE labels also appear as row thresholds, e.g. 'Rows 15 & Above - Covered' (134), 'Rows 14 & Above - Covered' (119, 121B), 'Rows 5 and above provide roof coverage' (405).
seat1_side_verbatim: PARK-WIDE BOILERPLATE, from RateYourSeats, appearing identically on every Yankee Stadium section page checked (103, 104, 115, 119, 120A, 120B, 121B, 125, 134, 136, 201, 203, 205, 236, 239, 305, 318, 320B, 334, 405, 418, 420B): 'When looking towards the field, lower number seats are on the right'. WARNING ON THE EXACT STRING: the page's template renders the noun as a slash-separated placeholder, so the raw extraction reads 'When looking towards the field/field/stage/field, lower number seats are on the right' - the repeated 'field/field/stage/field' is a RateYourSeats template artifact (baseball/football/concert/soccer variants), NOT part of the meaning. The load-bearing clause is 'lower number seats are on the right'. SO: facing the field, SEAT 1 IS ON THE RIGHT-HAND SIDE of the section, i.e. seat numbers increase from right to left as you look toward the field. PER-SECTION CORROBORATION ON BOTH HALVES OF THE PARK - this is the check the brief demands, because the boilerplate has been correct on one half and wrong on the other at two parks so far. RIGHT-FIELD half, section 103: 'The Yankees Bullpen is to the Right of Section 103 - Sitting in Seat 1 will have you right up against the wall overlooking the Yankees bullpen.' and 'To sit near the Yankees bullpen, sit in seat 1 on the right-side of Section 103.' The Yankees bullpen is on the center-field side of 103, which is to the viewer's right when facing the field from a right-field section - so seat 1 on the right, CONSISTENT with the boilerplate. LEFT-FIELD half, section 136: 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is to the Left of Section 136' together with 'Alternatively, sitting in a high-number seat in Section 136 will have you next to the Visitor's bullpen' and 'You can get a really good look into the bullpen when entering the row from the aisle at the left side of the row.' High seat numbers are therefore on the LEFT, so seat 1 is on the RIGHT - again CONSISTENT with the boilerplate. BLEACHERS, section 201: 'seats 1-15 (right side) have poorer views' - seats 1-15 explicitly identified as the right side, CONSISTENT. CONCLUSION: no half-of-the-park disagreement was found at Yankee Stadium; the boilerplate is independently corroborated in right field, left field and the bleachers. NO per-section question-and-answer text contradicting it was found. NOT CHECKED and therefore not guaranteed: the field-level Legends ring (sections 11-29) and the club/suite sections - no per-section seat-1 statement was located for those, so treat them as UNVERIFIED. known_obstructions: FOUL POLES: RateYourSeats, verbatim - 'Some fans have complained about the foul poles in Sections 107 and 132, while others complain about being obstructed by handicapped seating.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/107 , repeated on https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/136). Note this also flags HANDICAPPED SEATING PLATFORMS as an obstruction source - directly relevant to an accessible-seating guide. HIGH OUTFIELD WALL in the field-level outfield near center: 'The main issue here is how high the outfield wall is near these seats closer to center field. I have sat in the front row of sections closer to the left field corner, and the wall is very short and doesn't cause any viewing problems. But from my front row seat in Section 136, the wall was very high and cuts off nearly half the outfield when sitting back comfortably in my seat.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/136). CENTER FIELD SPORTS BAR / CENTER FIELD PLAZA blocks high bleacher rows: section 201 has 'obstructed views of left field due to the center field plaza and sports bar', section 239 warns that 'higher rows face obstruction from a center field sports bar' with 'Row 10 and below' recommended, and section 237 states 'Center Field Obstructions: Avoid rows higher than Row 10 in Sections 202 and 238' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/201 , /239 , /237). ROOF OVERHANG limits the upper view from covered rows: 'Rows 15 & Above - Covered' (134), 'Rows 14 & Above - Covered' (119, 120B, 121B), 'Rows 5 and above provide roof coverage' (405). PROTECTIVE NETTING, from the official netting page (https://www.mlb.com/yankees/ballpark/netting): the net spans 'between Section 011 on the 1st base/right field side of the Stadium and continues to Section 029 on the 3rd base/left field side'; it is 31 feet above the playing field wall behind home plate in Sections 018-021B, 'reducing in height as it approaches the dugouts'; 11'-6" from the top of the wall in front of Sections 017B and 022; 9 feet above the dugouts across that span, retractable up to 3 feet before games; approximately 14 feet above the field (roughly 11'-6" above surrounding walls) at Sections 014B-011 and 026-029; and 11'-6" above the wall behind the field-level photo wells at Sections 025 and 015A. The Yankees also state verbatim: 'Fans in these sections are still exposed to objects leaving the field of play, including bats and bat fragments, and thrown or batted balls; ticket holder assumes all risk of injury.' NOTE that the netting spans only the field-level ring (11-29) - the 100/200/300/400 level sections are behind and above it. BLEACHER BENCHES: the bleachers are 'Metal benches with no back support' and 'Completely uncovered' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/yankee-stadium/seating/sections/236).
